Sam Huang: Heads-up — Ignite POC showing inconsistent TTFT on short prompts. Median ~700ms but tails at 2.5s. Also seeing cache_miss metrics and occasional 429s during demo rehearsals. Can we swarm?
Priya Nair: On it. Are they on hosted or dedicated? Which model?
Sam Huang: Hosted. Config shows `redwood/gpt-3.5-x-16k@v2-quant` and default JS SDK. Concurrency small (4-8), payloads are single-sentence product lines. No explicit batching in app.
Marco Li: Share a log sample and recent request rate. If KV cache misses + no batching, TTFT will suffer on short prompts.
Sam Huang: Sample logs (sanitized): ```
[2026-03-21T09:04:11.021Z] req=ak-XXXX id=0x9b1 cpu=0.10s dispatch=0.01s runtime=0.65s first_token=0.68s tokens=1
[2026-03-21T09:04:12.450Z] req=ak-XXXX id=0x9c3 cpu=0.09s dispatch=0.02s runtime=2.4s first_token=2.45s tokens=1
METRIC: cache_miss prefix_hash=0x4c1f
WARN: rate_limit_trigger org_rate=6rps limit=5rps
```
Marco Li: Looks like they hit the per-org ramp throttle and cache isn't warming. Two common causes: 1) client not providing prefix-hint headers, 2) SDK older and not enabling batching.
Priya Nair: Their engineer said they used SDK 0.8.7. That might be the issue.
Jen O'Neill: 0.8.x didn't include `x-redwood-hint-prefix` or the default batching improvements. Recommend upgrade to >=1.1.0.
Sam Huang: Any quick server-side mitigations we can do while they upgrade?
Marco Li: We can enable `relaxed-prefix` matching for their org to increase KV hit rate for near-identical prompts. Also temporary burst quota bump to avoid 429s during the demo.
infra-bot: Org config update: org=ignite set relaxed-prefix=true (actor=infra, change_id=cfg-4821)
infra-bot: Quota change: org=ignite throughput=20rps window=120s (actor=billing, ticket=BL-998)
Priya Nair: Will notify the customer. Any caveats for relaxed-prefix?
Marco Li: It can slightly increase cache collisions for prompts that share leading tokens but diverge later; quality impact is minimal for their templates. We'll monitor via the evals dashboard.
Jen O'Neill: Also ask them to enable client-side batching: set `enable_batching=true` and `max_batch_latency_ms=30`. That reduces first-token variance for small requests.
Sam Huang: I'll push the upgrade + batching snippet now.
Priya Nair: I'll also flag a pre-demo load test for 5–10 minutes at 15rps to validate the quota bump.
Marco Li: If TTFT still bad after these changes, we'll check kernel selection and quant execution path on their active instances — there are rare cases where v2-quant falls back to slower kernels for short sequences.
Sam Huang: Great. Thanks team. I'll report back after the upgrade and load test. :thumbsup:
